                  <ns0:head>CHAP. IX.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p>NEvertheless, the dimness <ns0:hi>shall</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> such as <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> in her vexation <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The Words thus rendred contain a Mitigation of the foregoing Threatning: And so the sence of the Verse may be this, The Calamity of this Land and its Inhabitants shall be great, yet not such as that which was brought upon the Kingdom of the Ten Tribes by the King of <ns0:hi>Assiria,</ns0:hi> who at first indeed dealt more gently with them, but afterwards quite rooted them out, and carried them away into a dread<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful Captivity, from whence they were not to return, no not when the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> came into the World; for, after this Darkness, of which I have now spoken, there shall come a glorious Light, as it follows in the next Verse. The <ns0:hi>Dutch</ns0:hi> Interpreters take it in the same sence, and render the Words thus, <ns0:hi>But</ns0:hi> the Land <ns0:hi>that was distressed shall not be</ns0:hi> utterly <ns0:hi>dark<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned.</ns0:hi> To the same purpose they may be thus rendred, ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the <ns0:hi>Hebrew, But darkness shall not be (i. e.</ns0:hi> shall not abide or continue; for to <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> is sometimes put for to <ns0:hi>abide</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>continue to be,</ns0:hi> as 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 12. 14. <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 23. 5. <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 17. 4. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 8. 4.) <ns0:hi>unto her</ns0:hi> (to wit, the Land, which by the consent of Interpreters is understood here, as it was <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8. 21.) <ns0:hi>to whom</ns0:hi> this <ns0:hi>distress</ns0:hi> is or shall be. She shall be distressed and darkned, as I said before, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8. 22. but not irrecoverably, nor for ever. Some understand the Words to be an aggra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation of the Darkness or Misery threatned <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8. 22. ren<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dring the Words thus, <ns0:hi>for the dimness shall not be, &c.</ns0:hi> And so the sence is, This shall not be so sleight an Affliction as that which bes<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>l them by <ns0:hi>Pul,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 15. 19. nor as that which succeeded it by <ns0:hi>Tiglath-Pileser,</ns0:hi> who, at the desire of <ns0:hi>Ahaz,</ns0:hi> did about this time make another Invasion into the Land of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 15. 29. and was an heavier Stroke than the former, but this shall be far heavier than either of them. But the former sence seems better to agree both with the following Verse, and with <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 4. 13, 14, 15. where these Words are expoanded as a Promise, and said to be fulfilled by Christ's preaching the Gospel in these Parts.</ns0:note>, when at the first <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">In the first Invasion which the King of <ns0:hi>Assyria</ns0:hi> made upon <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> he <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">To wit, God, who is oft understood in such Cases, and who is here supposed to be the Author or Inflicter of this Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment. Or, it is an Impersonal Speech, <ns0:hi>he afflicted</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>was aflicted,</ns0:hi> than which nothing is more common in the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> Language.</ns0:note> lightly afflicted <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Either, 1. by <ns0:hi>Pul;</ns0:hi> or rather, 2. by <ns0:hi>Tiglath-Pileser,</ns0:hi> who at this time invaded and subdued these Parts, as is expressed 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 15. 29.</ns0:note> the land of Zebulun, and the land of Nephtali <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">These Parts are particu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />larly mentioned, because this Storm fell most heavily upon them; but under them the other Parts of the Land are understood by a common Figure called <ns0:hi>Synechdoche.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, and afterward did more grievously afflict her <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, 1. by <ns0:hi>Tiglath-Pileser;</ns0:hi> or rather, 2. by <ns0:hi>Shalmaneser,</ns0:hi> who took <ns0:hi>Sa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>aria,</ns0:hi> and carried <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> into Captivity, 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 17. 5, 6. Of which Calamity, though yet to come, the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet speaks as if it were past, as the manner of the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets is.</ns0:note> by the way of the sea <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">In that part of the Land which bordereth up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on the Sea, to wit, the Lake of <ns0:hi>Genesareth,</ns0:hi> which is very commonly called <ns0:hi>a sea,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 4. 18. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 21. 1. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and upon which the Portions of <ns0:hi>Zebulun</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Nephtali</ns0:hi> bordered.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> on this side.</ns0:note> beyond Jordan <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>on this side Iordan;</ns0:hi> for this Preposition is used both ways, and this Land might be said to be either <ns0:hi>beyond</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>on this side Iordan,</ns0:hi> in divers respects.</ns0:note> in Galilee <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> popu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lous.</ns0:note> of the nations <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>Galilee of the Gentiles,</ns0:hi> to wit, the <ns0:hi>Upper Galilee,</ns0:hi> so called because it bor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dered upon the <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi> But this last Clause, and the two foregoing Clauses, are otherwise rendred and interpreted by divers I earned men, as a Prophecy concerning the Light of the Gospel that should shine in those Parts, <ns0:hi>As at the first time</ns0:hi> (to wit, in the former Ages of the <ns0:hi>Israelitish</ns0:hi> Church and Commonwealth) <ns0:hi>he made the land of Zebulun and the land of Nephtali vile</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>contemptible</ns0:hi> (as he might be said to have done, partly by putting those People at so great a di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stance from his Sanctuary, partly by exposing them to some Calamities which other Tribes escaped, and partly by de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nying them those Honours and Privileges which he afford<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed to other Tribes, of which see <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 7. 52. <ns0:hi>Out of Galilee aris<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>th no Prophet;</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1. 46. <ns0:hi>Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?</ns0:hi> which was an eminent City of <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi>); so in <ns0:hi>the latter</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>last</ns0:hi> time (to wit, in the days of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> or of the Gospel, which are frequently so called in the Scri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ptures both of the Old and New Testament) <ns0:hi>he made it (i. e.</ns0:hi> he will make it, for the Prophet speaks of things to come as past, as he doth most commonly in this Prophecy) <ns0:hi>glorious</ns0:hi> (to wit, by Christs first preaching the Gospel in those Parts) <ns0:hi>in</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>towards the way of the sea</ns0:hi> (to wit, of <ns0:hi>Galilee</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Genesareth) beyond</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>on this side Iordan, in Galilee of the Gentiles.</ns0:hi> Which Interpretation I thought fit to propose, as deserving farther Consideration.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:572" />2 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 4. 16. Eph. 5. 14.</ns0:note> The people that walked <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">In <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 4. 16. it is <ns0:hi>sate.</ns0:hi> It notes not their gesture, but their State or Condition, they lived or abode. Onely <ns0:hi>walking in darkness</ns0:hi> is more perillous than sitting.</ns0:note> in darkness <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Expression is general, and so may well comprehend both the Darkness of Calamity, and the Darkness of Ignorance, and Idolatry, and Prophaneness, in which those Parts were eminently involved, by reason of their great distance from God's Sanctuary, and by their frequent Converse with the Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles, who bordered upon them, and of which this place is expounded, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 4.</ns0:note>, have seen <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Shall see at the coming of the <ns0:hi>Messiah.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Which notes both extreme, and dangerous, or deadly Darkness.</ns0:note>, upon them hath the light shined.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>k</ns0:hi> The People of God, <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> and especially those of them mentioned in the foregoing Verse.</ns0:note>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 Thou hast multiplied the nation <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Thou hast made good thy Promise to <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cerning the Multiplication of his Seed, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 15. 5. & 22. 17. by adding his Spiritual Seed unto the Carnal, by gathering in the Gentiles to the Jews, and making them both one People in Christ, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 10. 16. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2. 14. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> For in Scri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pture-account the Believing Centiles are the Seed of <ns0:hi>Abra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ham,</ns0:hi> as well as the Jews; of which see <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3. 7, 8, 9. Or, <ns0:hi>thou h<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>st magnified the nation,</ns0:hi> honoured them with peculiar Privileges above all other Nations, and especially with this transcendent Privilege, that the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi> and Saviour of the World should be born of them, and live among them; of which he speaks more fully, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 6, 7.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> to him.</ns0:note> not increased the joy <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Or, yet <ns0:hi>rot <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                              <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                           </ns0:gap>ncrea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed their joy.</ns0:hi> Which might very truly and fitly be said of the Jewish Nation, upon this occasion, partly because they did not rejoyce in the Conversion of the Gentiles, as they should have done, but murmured, and grieved, and stumbled at it; and partly because, through their perverseness and unbelief, that would be unto them an occasion of their ut<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter ruine, the Conversion of the Gentiles being attended with the Rejection of the Jews. But because this Transla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion seems not to agree with the following Words, which ascribe great Joy to them, some render the Words other<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wise; either thus, and <ns0:hi>wilt thou not encrease their joy?</ns0:hi> To which Question the next Words give an affirmative An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swer. So the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> Particle <ns0:hi>lo</ns0:hi> is put interrogatively for <ns0:hi>halo,</ns0:hi> as it is in many other places which I have formerly ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />served. Or thus, and <ns0:hi>hast increased to it,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> (to that Nation) their <ns0:hi>joy.</ns0:hi> For though the <ns0:hi>Hebrew lo</ns0:hi> be written like an Adverb, yet it may be read like a Pronoun, as it is both by Jewish and Christian Interpreters acknowledged to be in many places; of which see more in my <ns0:hi>Latin Synopsis.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: they joy before thee <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">In thy Presence, and in the Place of thy Worship; not with a Carnal and Worldly, but with a Spiritual and Reli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gious Joy, giving thee the Praise and Glory of all thy Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vours afforded to them.</ns0:note>, ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the joy in harvest <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">When men receive with great joy that for which they have laboured much, and long wait<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed. See <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 125. 5, 6.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>men</ns0:hi> re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />joyce when they divide the spoile <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">When, after a bloody Fight, and a glorious Victory, they come to take the Spoil.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> when thou breakest.</ns0:note> For thou hast broken <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This notes the Matter and Occasion of the foregoing Joy.</ns0:note> the yoke of his burden <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">His burdensom and heavy yoke, as <ns0:hi>the throne of ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liness</ns0:hi> is put for <ns0:hi>the holy throne, Psal.</ns0:hi> 47, 8.</ns0:note>, and the staff of his shoulder <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Either the Staff wherewith his Shoulders were smitten, or the Staff or Staves by which he was forced to carry Burdens upon his Shoulders.</ns0:note>, the rod <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Wherewith he beat him. Or, <ns0:hi>the scepter,</ns0:hi> the Power and Tyranny which he exercised over him.</ns0:note> of his oppressour <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Of all his Oppressors, but especially of Sin and of the Devil.</ns0:note>, as in the day of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jud. 7. 22. Chap. 10. 26.</ns0:note> Midian <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">When God destroyed the <ns0:hi>Midianites</ns0:hi> in so admirable a manner, and by such unlikely and contemptible Means, by Three hundred men, and they not fighting, but onely hold<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Lamps in their Hands, and sounding their Trumpets. Which was an eminent Type of Christ's conquering the Devil, and all his Enemies, by dying upon the Cross, and by the Preaching of a few unlearned and despicable Per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sons, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
